methods.name: Apply
methods.description:
Create or update a channel.

 A request that carries metadata.id of a channel in its organization
 updates that channel, and its slug changes only through rename. A slug
 the channel was renamed away from, named without the channel's id, is
 refused with FAILED_PRECONDITION carrying a google.rpc.ErrorInfo detail
 (domain "stigmer.ai"), because a write by a name that stops resolving
 after 30 days would later make a second channel:

   - SLUG_RENAMED — the slug was renamed: it still leads to the same
     channel for reading, but a write names its current slug. Metadata:
     slug (the one the request named).

methods.name: Create
methods.description:
Create a channel.

 Making a channel is a spending decision: conversations arriving over it
 call models on the channel's organization's own provider keys, and the
 providers bill the organization for them.

 A channel created without a name takes the slug `<agent slug>-<type>`
 (for example `variance-reporter-web`) and the name `<agent name> (<Type>)`.

 A slug another channel of the organization holds is refused with
 ALREADY_EXISTS. A slug another channel was renamed away from, which
 still leads to it for 30 days, is refused with ALREADY_EXISTS carrying a
 google.rpc.ErrorInfo detail (domain "stigmer.ai"):

   - SLUG_RESERVED — another channel held the slug until a recent
     rename, and it still leads there. Metadata: slug.

methods.name: Update
methods.description:
Update a channel: the fields update_mask names change, every other
 field keeps its stored value.

 The referenced agent and the channel's type are immutable; status
 (the link token, install facts) is never touched by updates. A mask
 naming a web channel's audience or the vaults replaces them whole: an
 empty audience makes the link organization-only, and empty vaults
 detach them (both fail closed).

 resource.metadata.id names the channel; apply finds one by slug. The
 slug changes only through rename, and a mask naming a field another
 door owns, or a path the channel does not have, is refused with
 INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the path.

 An update is refused with ABORTED carrying a google.rpc.ErrorInfo detail
 (domain "stigmer.ai"):

   - ETAG_MISMATCH — resource.metadata.etag is set and the channel changed
     since that etag was read: read it again and make the change again.
     No metadata.
   - WRITE_CONFLICT — the channel kept changing while the update was
     being saved: try again. No metadata.

methods.name: Rename
methods.description:
Rename a channel: change its slug, the name the CLI and getByReference
 address it by.

 The channel keeps its id, so everything that names it keeps working: a
 web channel's chat link names its id and does not change, and every
 answer names it by the new slug. The old slug keeps leading to the
 channel for reading for 30 days, during which no other channel of the
 organization can take it and this one can take it back; then it is
 released. A write that names the old slug is refused with SLUG_RENAMED
 (see apply). A slug another channel holds is refused with
 ALREADY_EXISTS, and one another channel was recently renamed away from
 with SLUG_RESERVED (see create).

methods.name: RotateLink
methods.description:
Rotate a web channel's link token.

 Generates a fresh server-side token for the channel's hosted chat link.
 The link becomes `/chat/<channel id>?k=<token>` and the previous link
 (tokened or plain) stops working immediately, including for visitors
 mid-conversation. Use this to kill a leaked or over-shared public link
 without disabling or deleting the channel. A Slack or WhatsApp channel
 has no link and is refused with FAILED_PRECONDITION.

 The token lives in status.web.link_token, so manifest applies never
 reset it. Rotation affects public-audience links only; org-audience
 access is governed by live organization membership instead.

methods.name: InitiateInstall
methods.description:
Start a Slack or WhatsApp channel's install flow.

 For redirect-installed providers (Slack) the output carries the
 provider authorization URL to redirect the installing user to, plus
 the single-use state that completeInstall verifies. For
 direct-installed providers (WhatsApp) the install runs to completion
 inside this RPC and the output carries completed=true instead. A web
 channel has nothing to install and is refused with
 FAILED_PRECONDITION.

 Refusals a client should branch on carry a google.rpc.ErrorInfo
 detail (domain "stigmer.ai") on the standard grpc-status-details-bin
 trailer, alongside the human-readable FAILED_PRECONDITION message:

   - WHATSAPP_NUMBER_ALREADY_CONNECTED — the WhatsApp Business number
     already serves an agent through this channel app (one agent per
     number per app). Metadata: display_phone_number (the occupied
     number), channel_app_id (the serving app).

methods.name: CompleteInstall
methods.description:
Complete a Slack channel's install flow.

 Called by the console after the provider's consent redirect, with the
 state from initiateInstall and the provider's authorization code. On
 success the channel's status carries the install facts and the
 channel begins serving (subject to spec.enabled). A web channel has
 nothing to install and is refused with FAILED_PRECONDITION.

 Refusals a client should branch on carry a google.rpc.ErrorInfo
 detail (domain "stigmer.ai") on the standard grpc-status-details-bin
 trailer, alongside the human-readable FAILED_PRECONDITION message:

   - SLACK_WORKSPACE_ALREADY_CONNECTED — the workspace already hosts
     an agent through this serving app (one agent per workspace per
     app). Metadata: team_name (the occupied workspace),
     channel_app_id (the serving app; empty = platform app).
   - CHANNEL_INSTALL_STATE_INVALID — the state parameter is missing,
     expired, or replayed; restart the install.
   - SLACK_ENTERPRISE_INSTALL_UNSUPPORTED — an Enterprise Grid
     org-wide install was attempted; install into a single workspace.

 Other refusals (unconfigured deployment, provider-refused code
 exchange) carry no reason: their message is the interface.

methods.name: Delete
methods.description:
Delete a channel.

 Full teardown: a web channel's link stops resolving and live guest
 tokens die on their next message; a Slack or WhatsApp channel's inbound
 events stop resolving, pending deliveries are abandoned, and its sealed
 provider credentials are deleted. The channel's configuration is gone.
 To pause serving while keeping it, update the channel with
 enabled=false instead.

methods.name: Reply
methods.description:
Reply to a conversation as the business, through the same number the
 agent serves.

 The message is durably recorded and attempted inline; the outcome
 reports the truth of the attempt. A staff reply on an agent-held
 conversation is an implicit takeover: the agent goes quiet until
 handBack. Replying requires an existing conversation — the customer
 must have written first; an unknown conversation answers NOT_FOUND.

methods.name: TakeOver
methods.description:
Take over a conversation: the agent goes quiet until handBack.

 Taking over also clears the needs-attention flag — the human arriving
 is the answer to an escalation.

methods.name: HandBack
methods.description:
Hand a conversation back to the agent, restoring automatic replies.

 The agent re-enters with the conversation context it missed while the
 human held control.

methods.name: ClearAttention
methods.description:
Clear a conversation's needs-attention flag without taking it over.

 The false-alarm dismissal: an escalation that needs no reply is
 cleared in place, never via a take-over-and-hand-back dance.

methods.name: Escalate
methods.description:
Flag this conversation for human attention.

 Non-blocking: the agent keeps serving while the flag summons humans.
 Repeated escalation is harmless; the latest reason wins.

methods.name: List
methods.description:
List an organization's channel conversations, newest activity first.

 Returns conversations across all of the org's channels the caller can
 view, optionally filtered to one channel. Entries carry participation
 state and the customer's display name.

methods.name: CountConversations
methods.description:
Count an organization's channel conversations that match a filter.

 The number behind a badge such as the inbox's "needs you": the same
 predicate list applies, over the same channels, so the count and the
 list it opens never disagree.

methods.name: GetConversation
methods.description:
Get one conversation's identity and participation state.

 The single-row read behind a conversation detail view: who holds
 control, whether the conversation needs attention and why, the
 customer's display name, and the activity clocks. Answers NOT_FOUND
 until the customer's first message creates the conversation.

methods.name: ListTimeline
methods.description:
List one conversation's timeline, newest first, one page at a time.

 The timeline contains customer-visible items only: inbound customer
 messages (including non-text kinds the platform cannot render),
 delivered agent replies, and operator or platform sends. Run
 internals never appear.

methods.name: GetMediaDownloadUrl
methods.description:
Mint a short-lived download URL for one inbound timeline item's
 media file (an image or document the customer sent).

 Answers NOT_FOUND when the item does not exist in this conversation
 or carries no ingested media (a text item, or media the platform
 declined to ingest).

methods.name: SendMessage
methods.description:
Send a business-initiated message to a recipient on a channel.

 The message is durably recorded and attempted once inline; transient
 failures are retried in the background. The outcome reports the
 truth of the inline attempt.

methods.name: ListTemplates
methods.description:
List the message templates available on a channel.

 Read live from the channel provider's registry (WhatsApp: the
 WABA's templates), lightly cached. The provider is the source of
 truth; entries carry its vocabulary verbatim.

methods.name: ListMessagingChannels
methods.description:
List the channels the caller can send business-initiated
 messages on.

 Everything the read needs derives from the caller's credential; an
 agent with no proactive-messaging channel receives an empty list.

methods.name: Get
methods.description: Get a single channel by ID.

methods.name: GetByReference
methods.description: Get a channel by its organization-scoped reference (org/slug).

methods.name: ListByAgent
methods.description:
List the channels of a specific agent, newest first, every type
 together. Returns only channels the caller has access to, optionally
 scoped to one organization via the request's org field.

 This is how the agent's console tab and the CLI find an agent's
 channels regardless of their slugs.

methods.name: List
methods.description: List channels with optional label filtering.

methods.name: GetAgentProfile
methods.description:
Get the public profile of the agent a web channel serves, by the
 channel's id.

 This is the resolution path for the hosted chat page: anonymous
 visitors (no Stigmer account, no token) resolve a chat link to the
 trimmed ChannelAgentProfile, never the full Agent, whose spec carries
 the system prompt and MCP wiring.

 Returns NOT_FOUND when the channel does not exist, is not a web
 channel, is disabled, has the org audience (anonymous callers must not
 be able to distinguish an org-internal link from a nonexistent one;
 use getAgentProfileForMember instead), or the link is locked and
 link_token does not match the channel's current status.web.link_token.
 The same NOT_FOUND answers when the channel's organization no longer
 exists. The cases are deliberately indistinguishable so an unshared,
 revoked, or rotated URL leaks nothing. Returns INVALID_ARGUMENT when
 channel_id is empty.

methods.name: GetAgentProfileForMember
methods.description:
Get the profile of the agent a web channel serves, as a signed-in
 organization member.

 This is the resolution path for the hosted chat page when a web
 channel has the org audience: the public getAgentProfile deliberately
 returns NOT_FOUND for such channels, so a signed-in member resolves the
 same trimmed ChannelAgentProfile through this authenticated RPC
 instead. Also resolves public-audience channels, so an authenticated
 caller can use one resolution path for any chat link.

 Returns NOT_FOUND when the channel does not exist, is not a web
 channel, is disabled, the caller is not a member of the channel's
 organization, the channel's organization no longer exists, or the
 channel is a public-audience channel locked with a link token (this
 tokenless path must not reveal a killed link's profile); the cases are
 deliberately indistinguishable so a chat link leaks nothing to
 non-members. Returns INVALID_ARGUMENT when the id is empty.

 taken from resource.

The channel carrying the new values, named by metadata.id. Only the
 fields update_mask names are read, so the others may be left empty; the
 result is validated as a whole.

The paths the update changes, as proto field names (spec.enabled,

 names every path an update may change.

Input for renaming any API resource: changing its slug.

 Used by resource-specific command controllers whose kind lets a slug
 change. Each controller's rename RPC accepts this shared input and returns
 the full updated resource. A resource's slug never changes through update
 or apply; rename is its only writer.

fields.description: ID of the resource being renamed.

fields.name: Slug

The new slug. Same format as metadata.slug, at most 63 characters: the
 longest a reference's org takes.

Input for rotating a web channel's link token.

fields.name: ResourceId
fields.description: ID of the web channel whose link token is being rotated.

fields.name: ResourceId
fields.description: ID of the channel to install.

methodTypes.name: InitiateChannelInstallOutput
methodTypes.description:
Output of the initiate-install RPC.

 Two install styles share this output. For redirect-installed providers
 (Slack) the caller redirects the user to authorization_url; the provider
 redirects back to the console, which completes the install with the
 completeInstall RPC. For direct-installed providers (WhatsApp) the
 install completes inside this RPC: completed is true and there is
 nothing to redirect to; refresh the channel to see its install facts.

fields.name: AuthorizationUrl
fields.description:
Provider authorization URL to redirect the installing user to
 (for Slack: the "Add to Slack" consent screen). Empty when the
 install completed directly.

fields.name: State
fields.description:
Single-use opaque state parameter bound to this install attempt.
 Empty when the install completed directly.

fields.name: Completed
fields.description:
True when the install completed synchronously inside this RPC
 (direct-installed providers). Clients branch on this field, never on
 provider knowledge of their own, so the server stays the single
 source of install-style truth.

fields.name: Code

methodTypes.name: ApiResourceReference
methodTypes.description:
Generic reference to any API resource.
 Used across resources to reference other resources (e.g., Vault, Agent, Skill).
 Canonical written format: "org/slug" (e.g., "acme/web-search", "acme/my-agent").

 A reference has three forms:
 - Written: by name (org and slug), by id, or by both. A write that carries
   both must have them agree, or it is refused naming both. A name is
   resolved to its resource's id when the referring resource is written.
 - Stored: org (the organization's id), kind, id and version. The slug is
   not stored, so a reference keeps pointing at the resource it meant when
   that resource is renamed, and never at a new resource that takes its old
   name after it is deleted.
 - Returned: as stored, with slug filled with the resource's current name.
   A reference whose resource was deleted is returned with an empty slug.

 The kind a reference names is the kind its field declares
 (reference_kind); a reference that carries another kind is refused.

 Every reference in a resource's spec is checked when the resource is
 written: the target must exist, and a target in another organization
 must be one the writing organization's parent shares with its child
 organizations (visibility_child_orgs) to be referenced at all. A blueprint may not be
 more visible than the skills, plugins and agents it references, so
 what a person can run they can also read. A reference that fails the
 check is refused at write, never at run.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization that owns the referenced resource, by slug or id.

 When non-empty: an organization slug (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens,
 starts with a letter, 2-63 characters; e.g. "stigmer", "acme-corp") or an
 organization id (org_<ulid>). The server stores the id, so a stored
 reference keeps pointing at its organization across a rename.

 When empty: the reference is relative — the server resolves it to the parent
 resource's organization at write time. All stored and returned references
 always have org populated (absolute form, the id).

 Use empty org for same-org references (the common case).
 An explicit other org is accepted only when that organization is your
 organization's parent and shares the resource with its children
 (visibility_child_orgs).

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: Kind of the referenced resource (e.g., SKILL, AGENT, PLUGIN).

fields.name: Slug
fields.description:
Resource slug (user-friendly identifier, unique within org).
 Format: lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, must start with a letter
 and end with a letter or digit (e.g., "web-search", "variance-reporter").
 Length: 2-63 characters.

 Written to name the resource; never stored; returned filled with the
 resource's current name, empty when the resource was deleted.

fields.name: Version
fields.description:
The version of a skill, a plugin or a subagent the reference asks for;
 every other kind ignores it.

 Formats:
 - empty or "latest": the latest version;
 - a tag (e.g. "stable", "v1.0"): the version the tag names;
 - a 64-character hash: that exact version, which never changes.

 When it is read: a skill or plugin reference is resolved at the start
 of each turn, so a reference without a hash follows each new push, and
 the run records the version it loaded (RunStatus.loaded_versions). A
 subagent reference is resolved once, when the agent that lists it is
 saved, and the saved reference carries the hash it resolved to.

fields.name: Id
fields.description:
The referenced resource's id: what a stored reference holds. Optional
 on write, where the slug may name the resource instead; an id no
 resource of the kind holds answers as a missing resource. At most 64
 characters.

methodTypes.name: GetChannelAgentProfileRequest
methodTypes.description:
Input for resolving a web channel's public agent profile.

 Identifies the channel by its id, the one identity a hosted chat link
 carries (`/chat/<channel id>`), plus the link token when the link
 carries one. A channel id never changes and is never reused, so a link
 cannot be broken by a rename of the channel's organization or captured
 by a later holder of that organization's name.

fields.name: ChannelId
fields.description: Id of the channel, from the hosted chat link.

fields.name: LinkToken
fields.description:
Link token from the chat link's `?k=` parameter.

 Required (and validated) only when the link has been locked with
 rotateLink; ignored for plain links.

methodTypes.name: ChannelAgentProfile
methodTypes.description:
ChannelAgentProfile is the public projection of the agent a web channel
 serves.

 Returned to visitors of the hosted chat page. It is deliberately
 trimmed: the full Agent resource carries the system prompt
 (spec.instructions) and MCP server wiring, none of which may leak to
 anyone-with-link callers. The profile carries only what the hosted chat
 page needs to render a header and start a session.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Id of the organization that owns the channel. The hosted chat page
 creates the visitor's session in it.

fields.name: Slug
fields.description:
Slug of the channel: its name within its organization, as the CLI and
 getByReference address it. The hosted chat link names the channel by
 its id, never by this slug.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: Human-readable agent name for the chat page header.

fields.name: Description
fields.description: Human-readable agent description for the chat page header.

fields.name: IconUrl
fields.description: Agent icon URL for the chat page header.

fields.name: AgentRef
fields.description:
The channel's agent reference (spec.agent_ref): the hosted chat page
 starts the visitor's session on exactly this reference, version
 included. This is a name, not a capability: session creation still
 requires an authorized token, and the edition's guest gate admits a
 session only on this channel's agent.

enumTypes.name: ChannelSendOutcome
enumTypes.description:
ChannelSendOutcome reports what happened to a business-initiated
 message on the inline delivery attempt.

values.name: accepted
values.description: Provider accepted the message.

values.name: queued
values.description: Transient failure; the platform retries in the background.

values.name: refused
values.description:
Terminal refusal; detail says why (caps, recipient policy, provider
 policy such as an expired 24-hour window). The caller should adapt,
 not retry.

enumTypes.name: ConversationControl
enumTypes.description:
ConversationControl names who may speak to the customer on a
 conversation's public lane.

values.name: control_agent
values.description: The agent serves the conversation (the default for every conversation).

values.name: control_human
values.description: A human holds the conversation; the agent is quiet until handback.

enumTypes.name: ChannelConversationListFilter
enumTypes.description:
ChannelConversationListFilter names the server-evaluated predicates the
 conversation list can be narrowed to.

values.name: filter_wants_human
values.description:
Conversations where a human action is wanted: flagged for attention,
 or human-held with the customer's last message still unanswered
 (needs_attention OR (awaiting_reply AND control_human)).

values.name: api_resource_version
values.description: Immutable version record tracking changes to an API resource.

values.name: grant
values.description:
One role given to one principal on one resource. Who holds what on a
 resource is the set of its grants.

values.name: identity_account
values.description: User account in the identity system.

values.name: api_key
values.description: Credential for programmatic API access.

values.name: invitation
values.description: Shareable link for joining an organization with a configurable role.

values.name: federation_issuer
values.description:
An outside issuer whose tokens Stigmer accepts for its own users
 (identity federation): its keys, its audience, and what its tokens get.

values.name: oauth_app
values.description: Registered OAuth application with an external vendor for outbound authentication.

values.name: team
values.description: Named group of an organization's people that access is shared with as one.

values.name: organization
values.description:
The boundary that holds people, Agents, Sessions and secrets
 together; nothing outside it sees them.

 Its id is a minted org_<ulid> that never changes; every organization-scoped
 resource names it by that id (metadata.org). Its slug is unique across the
 server and may change through rename; requests may name the organization
 by either.

values.name: platform
values.description: Singleton platform instance representing the Stigmer deployment.

values.name: agent
values.description: AI assistant with instructions, tools, skills, and a delegation model.

values.name: run
values.description: Single run of an agent within a session, tracking tool calls and responses.

values.name: session
values.description: Conversation thread between a user and an agent.

values.name: skill
values.description: Knowledge resource that provides domain-specific context to an agent.

values.name: channel
values.description:
A way people reach an agent: a chat link or website widget, a Slack
 workspace, or a WhatsApp number.

values.name: channel_app
values.description:
Customer-owned messaging-platform app (e.g. a Slack app) that
 channels can install through instead of the shared platform app.

values.name: routine
values.description:
A saved agent invocation, run on an optional schedule or fired by Run now
 or over the API, acting as its owner.

values.name: memory
values.description: Agent-proposed, user-confirmed fact the platform remembers about a person.

values.name: plugin
values.description:
An installed Agent Plugins package: one thing holding skills, agents,
 hooks and MCP servers, which agents and conversations list whole.

values.name: vault
values.description:
A person's or an organization's box of logins (matched by a tool's
 address) and secrets (matched by name) that runs use.

values.name: score
values.description:
One grade of a finished run: a person's thumbs or a free run-health
 check.

values.name: scoring_rule
values.description:
AI grading switched on for one agent: its sample rate, monthly spending
 limit and judge model.

values.name: eval_run
values.description:
One run of test cases on an agent, or on a plugin on the built-in
 assistant, optionally with and without a plugin.

values.name: eval
values.description:
A set of test cases for an agent: an evals/ folder in Claude Code's
 plugin-eval format, pushed whole.

values.name: environment
values.description:
A named sandbox setup: the packages installed in every sandbox a
 conversation using it runs in, and the hosts it may reach.

values.name: file
values.description:
A file uploaded once and named by its id: given to a conversation with
 a message, held in a conversation's resources, or kept by its uploader.

values.name: plan
values.description:
Catalog entry naming a bundle of entitlements and the terms that buy it.

 Platform-level: a plan belongs to no organization, so it carries no
 authorization scope and no owner. Immutable once created; a change of
 terms is a new Plan and the old one retires.

values.name: subscription
values.description:
An organization's binding to a Plan; at most one active per organization.

 System-created: the payment system drives its lifecycle, so it has no
 owner and grants no roles. Its reads and writes authorize on the
 organization through the billing permissions.

values.name: license
values.description:
A signed grant of entitlements to a self-hosting customer for a term.

 Platform-level: issued by the cloud's operators and verified offline by
 the Enterprise server, so the customer is a value inside the license
 (which may or may not name a cloud organization) and the kind has no
 authorization scope and no owner. Claims are immutable once signed; a
 renewal is a new License.

enumTypes.name: ChannelInstallState
enumTypes.description:
ChannelInstallState tracks a Slack or WhatsApp channel's install
 lifecycle.

 This is deliberately distinct from spec.enabled: enabled is the owner's
 serving switch; install_state is the observed state of the provider
 connection. Traffic is served only when installed AND enabled.

values.name: pending_install
values.description:
The channel exists but the provider install has not completed.
 No traffic is served in this state regardless of spec.enabled.

values.name: installed
values.description:
The provider install completed; credentials are stored and the
 channel serves traffic while spec.enabled is true.

values.name: revoked
values.description:
The provider revoked the installation (e.g. the Slack app was
 uninstalled from the workspace or tokens were revoked). The channel
 configuration survives; re-installing returns it to installed.

enumTypes.name: ApiResourceVisibility
enumTypes.description:
Visibility controls who can access an API resource.
 This is orthogonal to ownership - visibility is about access control,
 while ownership (org) determines who manages the resource.

 Key distinction:
 - Ownership: Which organization controls/manages the resource
 - Visibility: Who can access/use the resource

 All resources belong to an organization. Visibility determines which
 users, inside that organization or in its child organizations, can read
 the resource. No level reaches every
 account on the server.

 The visibility levels map to FGA tuples:
 - PRIVATE: no additional viewer tuples (owner-only access)
 - ORG: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer tuple (everyone in the
   org — the org role hierarchy flows downward, so owners, admins, members
   AND read-only viewers all satisfy the organization#viewer userset)
 - CHILD_ORGS: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer
   (everyone in every child organization of the owning organization)
 - PUBLIC: retired; see the value's own comment.

values.name: visibility_private
values.description:
Only the owner, explicitly granted principals, and — for blueprint kinds
 in the cloud edition — org admins can access.
 This is the default for personal and run-scoped resources.

 Org admins count as owners of blueprint kinds (agent, channel,
 skill, plugin), so a private blueprint stays
 manageable — and visible — to its org's admins. Personal kinds
 (sessions) stay creator-only.

values.name: visibility_public
values.description:
Retired. This level made a resource readable to every account on the
 server; it is refused at create and at updateVisibility for every kind,
 and every stored row that held it has been moved to visibility_org.
 Sharing across organizations happens through plugins (a copy is
 installed and owned) or, from a parent organization to its children,
 through visibility_child_orgs.

values.name: visibility_org
values.description:
Everyone in the owning organization can access (read) this resource —
 all org roles including read-only viewers (the role just-in-time provisioning
 grants by default). Running or otherwise spending against the resource
 still requires the org-level member-or-guest permissions
 (can_create_session / can_create_run_in); org visibility widens
 read, never spend.

 FGA tuple: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer
 (The tuple once targeted organization#member, which
 excluded viewer-role users; the authorization model no longer admits
 that shape.)

values.name: visibility_child_orgs
values.description:
Everyone in every child organization of the owning organization can
 read and run this resource: the shared catalog an organization offers
 the organizations under it (spec.parent_org). Child organizations
 created later gain access automatically, and no other organization
 does. Instances, sessions, runs and vaults are never shared
 this way: each child runs the shared blueprint inside its own boundary.

 Only valid for blueprint kinds with supports_child_orgs: true, and only
 in an organization that is not itself a child.

 FGA tuple: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer

enumTypes.name: ServiceTier
enumTypes.description:
ServiceTier selects the provider-side speed/service tier for a run's
 model calls.

 Providers spell this differently — Cursor exposes per-model "fast" variants
 at higher per-token rates, Anthropic and OpenAI expose service tiers — but
 the platform semantic is uniform: the tier is a deterministic, user-selected
 attribute validated against the model registry at create time. A tier is
 selectable for a model only when the registry prices it
 (pricingVariants.<tier>), so a selected tier is always billable.

 The load-bearing rule: UNSPECIFIED resolves to SERVICE_TIER_STANDARD — never
 the provider account default. The runner always sends the provider an
 explicit variant selection, so an out-of-band account setting can never
 silently change what a run pays (stigmer/stigmer#357).

values.name: SERVICE_TIER_STANDARD
values.description:
Standard tier: the model's base-priced configuration, requested
 explicitly.

values.name: SERVICE_TIER_FAST
values.description:
Fast tier: the model's fast variant, billed at the registry's fast
 variant rates.

 Valid only for models whose registry entry declares a fast pricing
 variant; refused at run create otherwise.

enumTypes.name: ThinkingMode
enumTypes.description:
ThinkingMode selects the model's extended-reasoning ("thinking") variant
 for a run's model calls — the second variant dimension alongside
 ServiceTier (stigmer/stigmer#772).

 Unlike the fast tier, thinking is NOT a separately priced dimension:
 Cursor bills thinking variants at the model's base per-token rates
 (verified against the live pricing page and 277 team-ledger events on
 2026-08-15 — thinking wire ids bill exactly base; thinking+fast bills
 exactly the fast variant rate). Thinking costs more only by generating
 additional reasoning tokens, billed as ordinary output. Selectability is
 therefore CAPABILITY-gated, not pricing-gated: ENABLED is valid only for
 models whose registry entry on the run's harness declares a
 thinking capability (capabilities.thinking or capabilities.adaptive_thinking),
 refused at create time otherwise. ENABLED means "the model reasons before
 it answers", in the form its entry declares: a fixed budget or adaptive
 depth.

 The load-bearing rule mirrors ServiceTier: UNSPECIFIED resolves to
 THINKING_MODE_DISABLED — never the provider account default. Several
 catalog default variants are thinking=true (claude-haiku-4-5), so an
 unpinned selection would silently follow an out-of-band account setting;
 the runner always sends an explicit thinking pin where the model declares
 the parameter. The one exception is a model whose entry declares
 capabilities.thinking_required: it always thinks, so an explicit DISABLED
 is refused at create and UNSPECIFIED runs with thinking on.

values.name: THINKING_MODE_DISABLED
values.description:
Extended reasoning off: the model's base variant, requested explicitly
 (thinking=false pinned where the model declares the parameter).
 Refused at run create for a model that requires thinking.

values.name: THINKING_MODE_ENABLED
values.description:
Extended reasoning on: the model's thinking variant, billed at base
 per-token rates (reasoning tokens bill as output tokens).

 Valid only for models whose registry entry on the run's harness
 declares a thinking capability; refused at run create otherwise.

enumTypes.name: ChannelAudience
enumTypes.description:
ChannelAudience selects who can chat over a web channel's hosted link.

 Unspecified is treated as org: a link reaches the internet only when
 public is chosen explicitly.

values.name: channel_audience_public
values.description:
Anyone with the link can chat, no Stigmer account required.
 Visitors are anonymous guests; suitable only for knowledge that is
 safe to expose to the entire internet.

values.name: channel_audience_org
values.description:
Only signed-in members of the channel's organization can chat.
 Membership is checked on every conversation turn, so access ends the
 moment a member leaves the organization. The right mode for
 org-internal knowledge agents.

enumTypes.name: ConversationLane
enumTypes.description: ConversationLane distinguishes customer-visible items from internal ones.

values.name: lane_public
values.description: The customer sees this item (their message, a delivered reply, a send).

values.name: lane_internal
values.description: Org-internal item (escalations, notes); the customer never sees it.

enumTypes.name: ConversationItemAuthor
enumTypes.description: ConversationItemAuthor names who authored a timeline item.

values.name: author_customer
values.description: The external customer.

values.name: author_agent
values.description: The serving agent.

values.name: author_teammate
values.description: An org human replying as the business.

values.name: author_platform
values.description:
Platform-authored conversation copy (e.g. the takeover
 acknowledgment), neither the agent's words nor a teammate's.

enumTypes.name: ChannelDeliveryStatus
enumTypes.description: ChannelDeliveryStatus is the delivery record lifecycle.

values.name: pending
values.description: Awaiting the run's terminal phase, or awaiting (re)claim.

values.name: delivering
values.description: Claimed by a delivery worker; provider I/O in flight.

values.name: delivered
values.description: Reply delivered to the provider.

values.name: failed
suppressed
values.description:
Withheld because a human held the conversation when the reply came
 due; the customer never received it.

enumTypes.name: ChannelReceiptState
enumTypes.description:
ChannelReceiptState is the provider-reported delivery progress of an
 accepted outbound message, as learned from delivery receipts.

values.name: receipt_sent
values.description: The provider accepted the message into its delivery queue.

values.name: receipt_delivered
values.description: The message reached the recipient's device.

values.name: receipt_read
values.description: The recipient viewed the message (or played it, for voice).

values.name: receipt_failed
values.description:
The provider could not deliver the message; receipt_detail and
 receipt_error_code carry the provider's verdict.

enumTypes.name: ChannelOutboundOrigin
enumTypes.description:
ChannelOutboundOrigin records which trust context authorized a
 business-initiated send.

values.name: channel_conversation
values.description:
The send came from a run created by an inbound channel
 message; the recipient must be a known sender on the channel.

values.name: operator
values.description:
The send was authored by an operator (console, CLI, SDK, a routine's
 run); any recipient, bounded by caps.

values.name: platform
values.description:
Platform-authored conversation-context copy (e.g. the takeover
 acknowledgment), neither the agent's words nor a human's.

values.name: participant
values.description:
A staff member's reply inside a live conversation, sent through the
 conversation-scoped reply command.

enumTypes.name: ChannelAttemptFailureKind
enumTypes.description:
ChannelAttemptFailureKind classifies WHY a send attempt reached
 status failed — and with it, whether the failure's stored explanation
 was authored for the conversation surface (attempt_detail) or is an
 operator-only diagnostic (last_error).

values.name: attempt_refused
values.description:
The provider terminally refused the send; attempt_detail carries
 the platform's mapped human explanation (e.g. the 24-hour
 customer-service-window copy for WhatsApp code 131047).

values.name: attempt_errored
values.description:
A technical failure (transport error, unexpected provider error,
 unresolvable credentials — exhausted retries or unattemptable at
 the first try). attempt_detail is EMPTY by construction; the raw
 diagnostic lives in last_error and never reaches the thread.

values.name: attempt_withdrawn

resourceDescription:
Channel is a way people reach an agent: a chat link, a Slack workspace or a WhatsApp number.

 The channel's type (spec.web, spec.slack or spec.whatsapp) says how
 people reach the agent. Every type records which agent serves the
 channel, whether serving is enabled, the vaults that supply the agent's
 tool credentials, and the per-turn run settings. A web channel is a
 hosted chat link (`/chat/<channel id>`) and the widget sites embed; a
 Slack or WhatsApp channel is a connection the provider delivers messages
 to, whose workspace identity and credentials come from the install flow
 and live in status. Disabling pauses serving and keeps the
 configuration; deleting tears it down. Deleting the agent deletes its
 channels. Channel operations never modify the referenced agent.

statusType.name: ChannelStatus
statusType.description: ChannelStatus contains system-managed state for a channel.

fields.name: VaultAttachers
fields.description:
Who attached each of this resource's vaults, by vault id: the account
 whose permission to use the vault each run checks when it has no
 person.

fields.name: InstallState
fields.description:
Install lifecycle of a Slack or WhatsApp channel's provider connection.
 Unspecified on a web channel, which has nothing to install.

fields.name: Web
fields.description: A web channel's link token.

fields.name: Slack
fields.description: Slack workspace install facts.

fields.name: Whatsapp
fields.description: WhatsApp Business number install facts.

fields.name: Audit
fields.description: Standard audit information (created_at, updated_at, created_by, etc.)

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAudit
statusNestedTypes.description: ApiResourceAudit contains both spec-level and status-level audit details.

fields.name: SpecAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's specification (desired state).

fields.name: StatusAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's status (actual state).

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAuditActor
statusNestedTypes.description:
ApiResourceAuditActor represents the entity that performed an action.

 This is the platform's single actor vocabulary: every "who did this"
 reference (created_by / updated_by, version-history applied_by / pushed_by,
 approval resolved_by_actor) uses this message, so actor rendering is
 uniform across all surfaces.

fields.name: Id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the actor.

fields.name: Avatar
fields.description: URL to the actor's avatar image.

fields.name: DisplayName
fields.description:
Human-readable display name (e.g. "Ada Lovelace"). Empty when unknown;
 renderers fall back to email, then id.

fields.name: Email
fields.description:
Email address of the actor. Empty when unknown or not applicable
 (e.g. machine accounts).

fields.name: MintedBy
fields.description:
The service account whose key minted the user token the actor acted
 through. Empty for every other credential, and on an actor that records
 no act (an account's profile lookup).

fields.name: CreatedBy
fields.description: Actor who created this resource.

fields.name: CreatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was created.

fields.name: UpdatedBy
fields.description: Actor who last updated this resource.

fields.name: UpdatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was last updated.

fields.name: Event
fields.description: Type of the last event (e.g., "created", "updated").

statusNestedTypes.name: SlackInstallStatus
statusNestedTypes.description:
SlackInstallStatus holds the facts observed when the Stigmer Slack app
 was installed into a workspace.

fields.name: TeamId
fields.description: Slack workspace (team) ID, e.g. "T0123ABCD".

fields.name: TeamName
fields.description: Human-readable workspace name at install time.

fields.name: BotUserId
fields.description:
Bot user ID minted by the install, e.g. "U0456EFGH".
 The identity the agent posts as; also how @mentions are recognized.

fields.name: GrantedScopes
fields.description: OAuth scopes granted to the installation.

fields.name: InstallerSlackUserId
fields.description: Slack user ID of the person who performed the install.

fields.name: InstalledAt
fields.description: When the install completed.

fields.name: ChannelAppId
fields.description:
ID of the ChannelApp the install went through; empty for installs
 of the platform's shared Stigmer app.

statusNestedTypes.name: WebChannelStatus
statusNestedTypes.description: WebChannelStatus is a web channel's server-generated state.

fields.name: LinkToken
fields.description:
Rotatable token protecting the channel's public link.

 Empty means the hosted chat link is the plain `/chat/<channel id>`,
 the behavior of every web channel created without a token. When set,
 the link only resolves with the matching `?k=<token>` query parameter;
 the rotateLink RPC generates a fresh value, killing the old link
 immediately. Applies to public-audience channels only (org-audience
 access is governed by live membership instead).

statusNestedTypes.name: WhatsAppInstallStatus
statusNestedTypes.description:
WhatsAppInstallStatus holds the facts observed when a WhatsApp Business
 number was connected through the Meta Cloud API.

fields.name: PhoneNumberId
fields.description: Phone number ID the install validated and bound, e.g. "106540352242922".

fields.name: DisplayPhoneNumber
fields.description: Human-readable phone number at install time, e.g. "+1 555 025 3483".

fields.name: VerifiedName
fields.description: WhatsApp Business verified display name of the number at install time.

fields.name: ChannelAppId
fields.description:
ID of the ChannelApp the install went through. Always set for
 WhatsApp: every WhatsApp channel installs through your own Meta app.

fields.name: InstalledAt
fields.description: When the install completed.
